documents.title: Referral request
documents.author: patient
documents.body: This is a little embarrassing to write. I've had irritation and itching in the private area for a few months and it's uncomfortable to sit. I would rather see a gynecologist than come in for this, is that ok? I haven't seen one since my hysterectomy.

documents.title: RE: Referral request
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Not embarrassing at all, and I'm glad you wrote. I've placed a gynecology referral and marked it to be seen soon. If you notice bleeding, a sore that won't heal, or a lump in the groin before then, let me know right away and I'll see you myself.

events.reason: Vulvar irritation and enlarging discolored lesion

documents.title: Gynecology consultation
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
GYNECOLOGY NEW PATIENT VISIT - 2/15/2023
Referred by: primary care

HPI: 69 yo, s/p TAH at 52 for fibroids, with several months of vulvar itching and a raw, sensitive feeling; sitting for long periods and walking any distance are uncomfortable. She also noticed a patch of discolored skin that has gotten bigger. Put off coming in out of embarrassment. Denies discharge, bleeding or recent sexual activity. On methotrexate and long-term prednisone for RA; recently evaluated by endocrinology for steroid side effects. Last Pap more than a decade ago (none needed after benign hysterectomy). Diabetes; blood pressure well controlled.

Meds: per PCP list (metformin, glyburide, lisinopril, amlodipine, HCTZ, omeprazole, prednisone, methotrexate, fluticasone-salmeterol, albuterol, aspirin, alendronate, calcium, D3).
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: External genitalia - 1.5 cm pale, thickened plaque with slightly irregular borders on the right labium majus. No ulceration. Remainder of the vulva without lesions. Vaginal cuff well healed. No inguinal lymphadenopathy bilaterally.

Procedure: After informed consent and local anesthesia, 4 mm punch biopsy of the plaque. Hemostasis with silver nitrate. Tolerated well.

Assessment: Vulvar plaque, rule out VIN or invasive carcinoma in an immunosuppressed patient.
Plan: pathology to follow; will call her with results. Topical care instructions given.

Outside OB/GYN group

conditions.label: Malignant neoplasm of vulva
conditions.note: squamous cell carcinoma, right labium majus

reports.text:
Specimen: skin, right labium majus, punch biopsy (4 mm).
Gross: one tan-white cylinder of skin, 0.4 x 0.4 x 0.3 cm, entirely submitted.
Microscopic: invasive keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma arising in thickened squamous epithelium. Tumor extends to the deep edge of the biopsy; depth of invasion cannot be fully assessed on this sample.
reports.conclusion: Right labium majus, punch biopsy: invasive keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma.

documents.title: Vulvar biopsy pathology
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body: Pathology from 2/15 vulvar punch biopsy received from gynecology: invasive keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma. Gynecology has referred her to gynecologic oncology and spoke with the patient this afternoon. Our referral also placed so it is tracked here. Flagged to PCP.

documents.title: Call to patient about biopsy
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called Beverly after gyn told her the biopsy showed cancer. She was teary but clear. Explained what squamous cell cancer of the vulva generally means, that the lesion is small and the groin felt normal, and that the next step is gyn oncology to plan surgery. Gyn onc consult is set for 3/6. Husband on the line part of the time. Offered a visit with me anytime; she will call. Discussed holding methotrexate around surgery - gyn onc and rheum will coordinate.

documents.title: Gynecologic oncology consultation
documents.author: gynecologic oncology
documents.body:
GYNECOLOGIC ONCOLOGY CONSULTATION
Date: 03/06/2023

69-year-old with biopsy-proven invasive keratinizing SCC of the right labium majus. Lesion 1.5 cm, unifocal, more than 2 cm from the midline structures. Groins clinically negative. Comorbidities: severe COPD with two intubations in 2021, CKD 3b, poorly controlled T2DM, RA on methotrexate and prednisone 10 mg daily.

Plan: radical local excision of the right vulvar lesion with 1-2 cm margins and right inguinal sentinel lymph node biopsy (lateral lesion). Anesthesia pre-op evaluation given her lung disease. Stress-dose steroids peri-operatively. Hold methotrexate the week before and after surgery (rheumatology agrees). Hold metformin day of surgery.

Allergies: none known.

Gynecologic Oncology, regional cancer center

events.reason: Radical local excision of vulvar cancer with sentinel node biopsy

reports.text:
A. Right vulva, radical local excision (oriented): invasive keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma, greatest dimension 1.5 cm, depth of invasion 2.1 mm. No lymphovascular invasion. Margins negative; closest peripheral margin 11 mm, deep margin clear. Background squamous epithelium with hyperplasia.
B. Right inguinal sentinel lymph nodes (2): two lymph nodes, negative for carcinoma on H&E and immunostains (0/2).
Pathologic stage: pT1b pN0. FIGO 2021 stage IB.
reports.conclusion: Invasive keratinizing SCC of the right vulva, 1.5 cm, DOI 2.1 mm, margins negative, 0/2 sentinel nodes; FIGO IB.

documents.title: Operative report and pathology summary
documents.author: gynecologic oncology
documents.body:
OPERATIVE REPORT - 03/21/2023
Procedure: radical local excision, right vulva; right inguinal sentinel lymph node biopsy with radiotracer and blue dye.
Anesthesia: general (LMA), stress-dose hydrocortisone given. Extubated in the OR without difficulty.
Findings: 1.5 cm plaque right labium majus; excised with 1.5 cm gross margins. Two sentinel nodes identified in the right groin.
EBL 50 mL. No complications. Observed overnight for her lung disease, discharged home the next day on usual medications; methotrexate to resume 1 week post-op.

PATHOLOGY (finalized 3/27): invasive keratinizing SCC, 1.5 cm, depth of invasion 2.1 mm, no LVSI, margins negative (closest 11 mm), sentinel nodes 0/2. FIGO stage IB.

Plan: no adjuvant treatment indicated. Surveillance exams every 6 months for 2 years, then every 6-12 months. Post-op visit in 2 weeks at the cancer center.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Three weeks after radical local excision and right groin sentinel node biopsy for a stage IB vulvar SCC. Op note and path reviewed: margins clear, nodes 0/2, no further treatment, surveillance with gyn onc. Post-op check at the cancer center went well.

She reports soreness at the incision, improving; groin site healed; walking more each day. No fever. MTX resumed. Breathing at baseline - no flare around surgery.

Exam: vitals as charted. Lungs distant without wheeze. Groin incision clean and dry. (Vulvar site deferred to gyn onc.)

A/P: Vulvar SCC, stage IB, s/p excision - surveillance per gyn onc. T2DM - A1c today. CKD - BMP. RTC June.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Routine follow-up. Healed from surgery and back to gardening from a stool. April A1c 8.8. Weight down a bit since last year. BP fine. No COPD flares. MTX labs today; copied to rheum.

Exam unremarkable for her: distant breath sounds, regular rhythm, no edema, feet intact.

Plan: continue meds; AWV in September.

documents.title: Gynecologic oncology surveillance visit
documents.author: gynecologic oncology
documents.body: Surveillance visit, 6 months after radical local excision and right inguinal SLNB for FIGO IB vulvar SCC. Asymptomatic. Exam: well-healed vulvar scar without lesions or thickening; groins without adenopathy; no lymphedema. No evidence of disease. Return 6 months.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Subsequent AWV.

Year in review: vulvar SCC found in February, excised in March, stage IB, no evidence of disease at gyn onc last week. No hospitalizations. Prednisone and MTX unchanged.

Function: independent in ADLs; uses rail on stairs; no falls this year. Lives with husband. Vision: early cataracts, followed. Hearing ok. PHQ-2 0.

Exam: vitals as charted. Lungs distant. Heart regular. Feet: sensation intact to monofilament, pulses present, no lesions.

Prevention: mammogram due 2024. Colonoscopy 2016 normal. Flu, updated COVID and the new RSV vaccine at a nurse visit in October - she is a good candidate with her lung disease. Labs today.
RTC 3-4 months.

documents.title: Fall vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Three vaccines today per PCP: high-dose influenza and RSV in the left deltoid (separated by more than an inch), updated COVID in the right deltoid. Screening questions negative. Pt tolerated well. Observed 15 min. Expect a sore arm; acetaminophen ok.

documents.title: Nephrology follow-up
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
Nephrology 10/24/2023. CKD 3b, creatinine 1.6-1.7 this year. Vulvar SCC treated surgically in March. PTH 172 today, calcium and phosphorus normal - secondary HPT stable on vitamin D3. Hemoglobin about 11, no ESA. Potassium normal on lisinopril. Reviewed sick-day rules again (hold metformin, lisinopril and HCTZ if vomiting or unable to drink). Return 1 year.

Outside Nephrology Group

documents.title: Rheumatology follow-up
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body: RA follow-up 11/14/2023. Methotrexate held around vulvar surgery in March, resumed without flare. Joints: no synovitis. Patient again declines a prednisone reduction for now. Monitoring labs fine. Continue methotrexate 15 mg weekly, prednisone 10 mg daily. 12 months.

documents.title: Diabetic eye examination
documents.author: optometry
documents.body: Dilated diabetic eye examination 12/5/2023. Corrected VA 20/30 OD, 20/25 OS. Cataracts mild, stable. Fundus: no diabetic retinopathy, maculae flat. Return in one year.
